how_it_wins:
Land one commander, let it tax every card that moves, then end the game one of two ways. Shabraz takes a +1/+1 counter and 1 life per card you draw. Brallin takes a +1/+1 counter and deals 1 damage to each opponent per card you discard. A seven-card wheel pays both seven times (stack 001: Windfall makes two 10/10s and takes every seat to 33).

THE WHEEL has two proved shapes. With Consecrated Sphinx out, Wheel of Fortune draws you 49 and the cleanup discard of 42 fires Brallin until all three opponents are at 0 (stack 009). That is the one checker-passed table kill. With Razorkin Needlehead and Torbran out, the same Wheel deals 21 to each opponent from their own draws, with no commander on the board (stack 011: 40 to 19). With Brallin out too, each card you discard adds 3, so seven discards finish it: 21 + 21 = 42. That sum is arithmetic across two stacks, not a stack. Six discards leave every seat at 1.

TWENTY-ONE is the stated ending, and it is UNPROVEN. Shu Yun, Embercleave, Blade Historian and Akroma's Will each give double strike, and no passing stack resolves combat with any of them. By arithmetic a 10/10 double-striker deals 20, one short; Embercleave's +1/+1 or Knowledge Is Power closes it. Count before you swing.

What has to be true on the turn you go. A commander has survived a turn cycle, or Needlehead and Torbran are both down. The wheel or the double-strike piece is in hand with the mana for it. A shield is up: Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free with a commander out, and Grand Abolisher stops spells on your turn. Until then, hold the wheel (game 002).

The board picks the road. Shabraz flies and every draw engine feeds him. Brallin and Needlehead are red, so Torbran adds to their damage and never to Shabraz's.

What the table misreads: a loot deck, two 3/3s and a 2/2. One wheel later every seat is down 7, or down 21.
mulligan:
Keep a hand that casts a commander on time and does something while it waits. Your rule from game 002: at most one wheel, and at least one creature or one ramp piece. The goldfish mulligans on lands alone (two to five) and keeps its first seven in 79.2% of games. Of its kept hands, 81.9% pass your rule, so one kept hand in five still needs your eye.

Lands. In 10,000 first sevens, 1,972 had one land or none, 2,965 had two, 2,904 three, 1,569 four and 590 five or more. Land drops hit on turn 4 in 80.3% of games and on turn 5 in 70.9%. Keep two lands only with a rock: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Azorius or Izzet Signet, Talisman of Creativity.

Check red, the short colour: 30 land sources against a target of 36. On curve with rocks it is 0.882, against W 0.907 and U 0.951. Brallin needs {R}, Needlehead {R}{R}, Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation {R}{R}{R}. Shabraz needs {W}{U}. Thundering Falls always enters tapped; Sundown Pass enters tapped as your first or second land.

Cards that make a keep: Sol Ring, a Signet, Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Kitsa, Faithless Looting, Stoneforge Mystic (she finds Lightning Greaves). Shark Typhoon is never dead: cycle it early for {1}{U}, or late for a big Shark.

Ship lands and wheels with no creature or rock. A wheel does nothing early: the goldfish holds a mean of 0.614 dead wheels in hand on turn 1 and 0.611 on turn 2. Do not keep for Needlehead, Torbran, Blade Historian or Embercleave. Needlehead on turn two is a 2/2 that pings each seat once a round and draws the first removal spell; it is a wheel-turn card.

Gemstone Caverns: off the draw, it can start on the battlefield making any colour, for a card from your hand.

combo_lines.001:
It turns on timing. Windfall's discard and draw are one resolution, and nobody gets priority inside it. All fourteen triggers wait until Windfall is in the graveyard, then you order them. Brallin is still a 3/3 through every draw.

What it proves: one Brallin trigger per card you discard. The opponents' discards pay nothing. Seven discards are 7 to each seat; seven draws are seven counters and 7 life on Shabraz. Brallin's half of a wheel is your hand size, not the table's. Razorkin Needlehead is the card that charges the table for its half (stack 011).

What it does not prove: anything about combat. Two 10/10s are 20 each with double strike, by arithmetic, and no stack on this list resolves the swing.

Three cards in the hand shown are no longer in the 99. They were discarded and did nothing in the line.
combo_lines.004:
It turns on Artist's Talent's level 3 being a replacement applied to each damage event on its own. Brallin's seven triggers are seven events, 1 + 2 = 3 each. Magmakin Artillerist's single trigger for the batch is one event, 7 + 2 = 9. Each opponent takes 30, 40 to 10.

What it proves: a per-event bonus pays many small pings more than one large blast. The extra 2 is dealt by Brallin or Magmakin, never by the Talent. By the same oracle text Needlehead's pings are noncombat events too; no stack has the Talent beside it.

What it does not prove: a kill. Each seat keeps 10, which needs a second wheel or a swing. Shabraz is not on this board, so the draw half is unpriced. Level 3 costs eight mana across the three levels, each gained as a sorcery, so the Talent is a two-turn setup.

Three cards in the hand shown are no longer in the 99. None of them acts.
combo_lines.005:
It turns on Torbran adding 2 to each separate damage event from a red source. Brallin is red, and his seven triggers are seven events: 3 each, 21 to every opponent.

What it proves: Torbran turns seven discards into 21 per seat. The stack's own title says the rest: not a kill from 40. This is the discard half of the Needlehead wheel; stack 011 is the draw half.

What it does not prove: the 30 to one opponent. That blast came from a card on the board that is no longer in the 99, so read the 21 per seat and drop the 30. Combat was scoped out. Whether Torbran's +2 on Brallin's strikes counts toward 21 commander damage is still open. Torbran never adds to Shabraz, who is white and blue.

One other card in the hand shown is no longer in the 99 and does nothing here.
combo_lines.007:
It turns on who orders the replacement effects. The damaged player orders them, not you. One Brallin ping under Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation can be 8, 10, 12 or 18 per seat. Each opponent applies both multipliers before Torbran's +2 and takes 8.

What it proves: price the smallest result. With all three out, every ping is at least 8 to each seat. Assuming each opponent minimises, five discards are 40 per seat by arithmetic. The discard came from Kitsa's loot, so one loot pays Brallin a counter and pings the table. Every card on this board is in the 99. Needlehead is a red creature, so the same ordering applies to its pings by oracle text; no stack has it under the multipliers.

What it does not prove: combat. Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation multiply commander combat damage by oracle text, and no stack resolves it. All the damage here is noncombat, so none of it counts toward 21.
combo_lines.008:
It turns on Lae'zel replacing each counter placement once per trigger. Every Brallin trigger puts two counters, and so does every Shabraz trigger.

What it proves: five discards and seven draws make Brallin 13/13 and Shabraz 17/17. The damage stays 5 per seat, because Lae'zel changes counters, not damage. Windfall draws everyone the largest hand discarded. Here that was an opponent's seven, so you drew seven off a hand of five.

What it does not prove: the swing. A 17/17 Shabraz with double strike is 34 to one seat by arithmetic, and no stack resolves it. Lae'zel is one card: 7.1% of opening sevens, drawn by turn six in 18.1% (deck-audit).

One card in the hand shown is no longer in the 99 and does nothing here.
combo_lines.009:
It turns on Consecrated Sphinx turning the table's draws into yours. Wheel of Fortune makes each opponent draw seven. That is 21 Sphinx triggers and 42 cards, plus your own seven. Shabraz ends 52/52 and you gain 49.

Then it turns on cleanup. You hold 49 cards, so cleanup discards 42 and fires Brallin 42 times. Triggers in cleanup open a priority window. After the 40th, all three opponents are at 0 and lose at once. No combat, and no mana after the Wheel.

What it proves: the one checker-passed table kill on the current 99. The basic Island on the board is not in the deck. It only paid mana.

What it does not prove: that the table lets it happen. Sphinx costs six and has to survive a turn cycle in front of everyone. Brallin is the half that kills; Shabraz's 52/52 is surplus. Your library needs 49 cards to draw. Grand Abolisher stops spells on the Wheel turn. Forge's AI held Wheel of Fortune in its cast proof, so only paper games will test this line.
combo_lines.010:
It turns on Kitsa's power. The copy ability needs power 3 or more, and Kitsa is a 1/3. She needs two prowess triggers this turn: Arcane Signet earlier, then the Wheel itself. The copy resolves first (discard three, draw seven), then the original discards those seven and draws seven more.

What it proves: one cast, two wheels. Ten discards pay Brallin ten times, so 10 to each seat and a 13/13. Fourteen draws pay Shabraz fourteen times, so a 17/17 and 14 life. The second wheel discards a full hand, so a short starting hand still pays twice. Each opponent also draws fourteen, which under Needlehead and Torbran would be 42 per seat by arithmetic; no stack has Needlehead on this board.

What it does not prove: a kill. Each seat keeps 30. The line costs the Wheel's {2}{R}, Kitsa's {2} and a noncreature spell cast earlier in the turn.

One card in the hand shown is no longer in the 99; it plays no part.
combo_lines.011:
It turns on Needlehead triggering per card drawn, not per instruction. "Draws seven cards" is seven separate draws for each opponent, so 21 triggers wait until the Wheel is in the graveyard, then go on the stack together. Needlehead is a red source, so Torbran adds 2 to each: 3 per trigger, 21 per seat, 40 to 19.

What it proves: the table's half of a symmetrical wheel is damage. Your own seven draws trigger nothing, and both commanders are in the command zone: this line needs neither. The Wheel was your last card, so you discarded nothing. With Brallin out, each card you discard adds 3 more per seat under Torbran (stack 005's shape).

What it does not prove: a kill. Each seat keeps 19. The sum that kills at seven discards, 21 + 21, is arithmetic across two stacks; no stack holds both halves. Nor does it prove the 2/2 lives: Needlehead and Torbran must sit on the battlefield before the Wheel, in front of the table. Only a card drawn counts; a card put into hand any other way triggers nothing.
combo_lines.012:
It turns on cycling being a discard paid as a cost. Paying it triggers Brallin and Marauding Mako, and Shark Typhoon's own trigger works from the graveyard. All three resolve before the cycling draw, and the draw then triggers Shabraz.

What it proves: one card at instant speed pays all three. Brallin, Mako and Shabraz each take a counter, every opponent takes 1, you gain 1 and draw 1, and Brallin's {R} can give the flying Shark trample. You can do it at an opponent's end step or in response to removal, which is the window a sorcery-speed sweeper leaves open.

What it does not prove: the Shark's size. The 4/4 for X=4 is the card's official ruling, taken as an input; the stack does not derive it. Cycling is not casting, so Shu Yun, prowess and the card's own enchantment mode do not see it. And it is a value turn, not damage: 3 across the pod.

threat_assessment:
Three games are logged, none on v2.2.0. Every table read below is an assumption.

WHEN YOU STOP BEING IGNORED. On turns one to four the table sees a loot deck and two 3/3s. Five signals end that read.
- Counters on a commander. The goldfish reads a mean of 9.395 commander counters by turn six and 22.55 by turn eight (a ceiling: no removal).
- A wheel resolving with a commander out. Stack 001: every seat to 33 and two 10/10s.
- Consecrated Sphinx beside Brallin. That board is stack 009, the table kill.
- Razorkin Needlehead beside Torbran. A 2/2 that pings each opponent on every draw; one Wheel makes it 21 per seat (stack 011).
- Torbran or a level-3 Artist's Talent beside Brallin: 21 or 30 per seat off seven discards (stacks 005, 004).
WHAT TO DO. Put the loudest piece down last. Cast Sphinx or Needlehead the turn the wheel follows, or behind Grand Abolisher. Land a commander on a quiet turn behind Lightning Greaves.

COUNT THEIR MANA FIRST. Assumption: a blue seat with two open holds a counter, and four open holds removal. Match the shield to the threat.
- Flawless Maneuver: free with a commander out; indestructible only. Exile, bounce and -X/-X go through.
- Akroma's Will, both modes with a commander out: protection from each colour and indestructible. Colourless removal goes through.
- Deflecting Swat: free with a commander out; it gives a targeted spell or ability a new target.
- Loran's Escape; Robe of Stars ({1}{W} phases the carrier out); March of Swirling Mist.
- Negate, Stubborn Denial, Izzet Charm: noncreature spells only. Denial is a hard counter once you control a creature with 4 power.
- Grand Abolisher: no spells, and no artifact, creature or enchantment abilities, on your turn.

THE GREAVES TRAP. Shroud stops your own targeting too. On a commander in Lightning Greaves you cannot attach Embercleave, take Shu Yun's double strike, place Inti's counter or use the commanders' cross-grants. Move Greaves first (equip {0}), or win with untargeted cards: Blade Historian, Akroma's Will, Knowledge Is Power, Gratuitous Violence, Jeskai Ascendancy.

TWO TAXES. Each cast from the command zone costs {2} more for every earlier one. Command Beacon puts a commander in hand, so that cast pays no tax. Needlehead and Torbran need no commander.

WHAT YOU CANNOT ANSWER. Nothing in the 99 exiles a graveyard (deck-audit). Incendiary Command is the one sweep. Prismari Command and Chaos Warp handle artifacts, and Get Lost and Chaos Warp handle enchantments.
matchups:
SWEEPER CONTROL. You are the beatdown; the long game is theirs. Commit one commander and keep the other in the command zone as the rebuild. Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will beat a destroy wipe only. Against exile or bounce, hold Negate, Stubborn Denial or Izzet Charm, or phase out with March of Swirling Mist. After the wipe, cycle Shark Typhoon at their end step: a flier back on the table at instant speed (stack 012).

COUNTERSPELLS AND DRAW-GO (Steven, game 001). A symmetrical wheel refills their hand too. Without Sphinx or Needlehead out, prefer the one-sided refills: Tolarian Winds and Fateful Showdown redraw only your hand, and Collective Defiance's wheel mode targets one player. With Needlehead and Torbran out, their seven fresh cards cost them 21 (stack 011), and every extra card they draw costs 3. On the kill turn, Grand Abolisher stops every spell they hold, and a counterspell cannot touch triggers.

GO-WIDE TOKENS (Stuart's zombies, game 001). Your one sweep is Incendiary Command, 2 to each creature, yours included; it kills Needlehead. Go over the board. Shabraz flies, and his {W/U} gives a Human flying: Brallin and Needlehead are both Humans. Brotherhood Regalia makes a commander unblockable. Shabraz gains 1 life per draw, Bard has reach and vigilance, and a cycled Shark is a flash-speed flying blocker. Hit the token seat first.

COMBO. Held answers lose value against combo, so spend them. Hold one of Negate, Stubborn Denial or Izzet Charm rather than tap out for an engine. Grand Abolisher protects your turn only. Your clock will not outrun them. The goldfish's median kill is turn 7, against one seat with no blockers, and it kills by turn six in 32.5%.

STAX. Race it. A spell tax hits Shu Yun, Jeskai Ascendancy and Artist's Talent, which want several noncreature spells a turn. With Torbran out, Needlehead ({R}{R}) and Wheel of Fortune ({2}{R}) are five mana for 21 per seat. Chaos Warp and Get Lost answer the piece; Prismari Command destroys an artifact. Lightning Greaves at equip {0} survives an equip tax that Embercleave's {3} does not.

GRAVEYARD DECKS. Nothing in the 99 exiles a graveyard, and every wheel fills every yard. Loot instead: Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Kitsa, Mary Read and Anne Bonny and Teferi, Master of Time fill only yours.

TWO SEATS IN ONE TURN. Each 21 commander damage removes one opponent and leaves two with shots at you. The Sphinx wheel (stack 009) is the one proved line that removes all three.
